text.p: Britain's rail operator Railtrack Plc reported pretax profits of 346 million pounds ($565.4 million) in the year to March 31, 1997, less than a year after it was privatised by the UK government.

Railtrack, in charge of the country's wide network of railway tracks, reported a 15 percent increase in its operating profit to 339 million pounds and showed an improvement in of earnings per share to 58.4 pence share from 53.8 pence, on a proforma basis.
The company's turnover was up to 2.44 billion pounds from 2.3 billion in the previous year. It recommended a dividend of 22.1 pence per share.
Railtrack, under pressure to spend more on its infrastructure for the benefit of passengers, recently unveiled a plan to invest about 15 billion pounds over a period of 10 years.
"The tangible improvements in service which we promised are being delivered and we continue to pursue our ambition to create the world's best railway," said group chairman Sir Robert Horton.
